blocks.text: This feature is in limited availability and requires a Private Access (ZPA) Federation license. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.

Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation enables organizations to provide seamless Zero Trust access to private applications across independent Private Access tenants. By establishing a secure trust relationship between a host tenant (i.e., the application owner) and a guest tenant (i.e., the user organization), administrators can eliminate the need for complex site-to-site VPNs, manual account duplication, or cumbersome IP address allowlisting. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations.
Before understanding the B2B Federation processes, Zscaler recommends you are aware of the following:

blocks.item: Prerequisites
To use B2B Federation, ensure the following:
Both the host and guest partners must:
Have a Private Access tenant.
Complete migration to Authentication Service for admins. To learn more, see Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to Authentication Service.
Have Zscaler Experience Center enabled. To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Experience Center?
This feature is only supported for Experience Center.
Partners must have an active Private Access license to use B2B Federation, but only the host partner needs a Federation license to share applications with a partner.
Have the Partner permission enabled in their admin role. To learn more, see Configuring Administrator Roles.
The host partner must have the Federate Application permission enabled in their admin role. To learn more, see Configuring Administrator Roles.
Both the host and guest partners must originate from the same cloud. For example:
A tenant (i.e., tenant 1) from private.zscaler.com can only federate another tenant (i.e., tenant 2) from private.zscaler.com.
A tenant (i.e., tenant 1) from zpatwo.net can only federate another tenant (i.e., tenant 2) from zpatwo.net.
To learn more about your cloud, see Customizing Your Account Settings.
App Connectors and Private Service Edges are upgraded to version 24.298.1 or later.
Zscaler Client Connector is upgraded to the following versions per OS:
Windows versions:
4.7.0.88 or later
4.6.0.282 or later
macOS version 4.5.2.98 or later
Android version: 3.10 or later
Linux version: 4.2 or later
iOS version 4.4.1 or later
Ensure Use Tunnel SDK version 4.3 or above is enabled in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal. To learn more, see Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles.

The AUP defines the terms and conditions for sharing applications between organizations. To learn more, see Fair Use and Compliance.

The partner that owns the private applications.
The admin of the host partner organization.

blocks.text: The following use cases highlight how B2B Federation can be used across various business and compliance scenarios:

blocks.item: Native B2B Partner Collaboration

Streamline secure access for external partners (e.g., vendors, suppliers, and strategic consultants) to private applications hosted within your environment. This model is ideal for high-frequency collaboration where external users require secure, least-privileged access.
The following summary details the native B2B partner collaboration use case:
Accelerated onboarding: Grant partners immediate access to necessary resources without the administrative overhead of traditional network configurations.
Granular authorization: Enforce host-defined access policies (e.g., device posture and user identity) to ensure external users reach only specific application segments, preventing lateral movement.
Administrative efficiency: Reduce overhead by allowing guest tenants to manage their own users and groups while the host tenant retains control over access policies.
For example:
Granting subcontractors access to project management portals or inventory systems.
Allowing strategic suppliers to securely interact with internal supply chain management tools.
Mergers, Acquisitions, and Divestitures

B2B Federation provides the agility required to maintain business continuity during organizational restructuring. It allows entities to remain operationally independent while securely sharing resources.
The following use case information applies to mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures:
Mergers and Acquisitions
Pre-merger due diligence: Provide temporary access to financial systems and audit tools for the acquiring team to assess the target company's data securely.
Post-merger integration: Maintain secure access to shared applications across both organizations during the transition period.
Divestitures
Secure separation: Ensure a divested business unit maintains temporary access to shared corporate services (e.g., HR or Finance systems) while transitioning to its own infrastructure.
Cross-entity collaboration: Facilitate long-term R&D or operational partnerships between the parent company and the independent divested entity.
Multi-Tenant and Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) Environments

This use case supports organizations that operate across multiple Private Access tenants due to geographic segmentation, business unit siloing, or managed service models. The following use case information applies to multi-tenant and MSSP environments:

Inter-unit resource sharing: Large enterprises with siloed IT environments can securely share tools (e.g., global ERP systems) between North American, European, and Asia-Pacific tenants without replicating infrastructure.

MSSPs: Service providers can manage multiple client tenants and enable secure interaction between them, such as allowing MSSP engineers to access Security Operations Center (SOC) dashboards across different client environments.
Federal and Public Sector Compliance

Federal organizations often maintain separate Private Access tenants to satisfy specific data sensitivity and compliance requirements (e.g., FedRAMP High vs. Moderate). B2B Federation enables secure cross-tenant communication while maintaining regulatory boundaries. The following use case information applies to federal and public sector compliance:
Intra-agency collaboration: Securely share mission-critical data and reporting tools between federal agencies operating at the same classification level (e.g., FedRAMP High to High).

Federal-to-commercial connectivity: Enable federal users to securely access commercial applications hosted within a commercial Private Access tenant, ensuring that federal identity and posture requirements are enforced.
Compliance adherence: Maintain strict data sovereignty and audit trails for all cross-tenant transactions, meeting federal oversight standards.

blocks.text: The process of establishing trust between a guest partner and host partner for access to shared resources is called the Zero Trust Partner Federation process, and requires the host partner to share an access token with a guest partner. The guest partner then verifies the token and establishes trust.
The federation process is as follows:

blocks.item: Establish mutual trust between Private Access tenants using a secure token exchange. Any business partner (guest or host) can initiate B2B Federation. To learn more, see Configuring Business-to-Business Federation.
The host partner publishes the private app segments with the guest partner. The host shares the required applications with the guest. To learn more, see Federating Defined Application Segments.

The guest partner enforces Zero Trust access by configuring an access policy for the application segments published by the host partner. To learn more, see Configuring Access Policies and Configuring Timeout Policies.

blocks.text: B2B Federation only supports user-to-application access between two partners using Zscaler Client Connector.

Federated applications are defined application segments that are created, owned, and managed by the host partner, and then shared with guest partners. Federated applications are used in combination with federated access policies for access to shared resources. Only application segments with hostname-based configurations can be federated. Wildcards in hostnames are supported, for example:

blocks.item: app.partner.example.com
*.partner.example.com

blocks.text: B2B Federation does not support overlapping domains across multiple host partners. If two host partners (e.g., host 1 and host 2) are both federated with a common guest partner (i.e., guest 1), they cannot share the same application domain (e.g., *.app.com). The domain ownership is exclusive (i.e., only the first host partner that registers a domain is permitted to use it within the federation). If a second host partner attempts to configure federation using an already-registered domain, the federation setup will be blocked and cannot proceed. This restriction ensures domain uniqueness and prevents conflicts in application access routing across federated partners.
To learn more, see About Applications and Federating Defined Application Segments.

Access policies for federated applications facilitate secure, controlled access between two partners, specifically for selected application segments. Access policies for federated applications allow the Federated B2B partners to establish a Zero Trust connection with access control. To learn more, see About Access Policies Defined by My Tenant and About Access Policies Defined by Partners.

Only the guest partner admin can define, configure, and modify access policies to allow guest partners access to the shared host partner applications. The host partner has read-only access to view the policies configured by the guest partner.

Timeout policies define how long a guest partner user's access or session to a federated application remains valid before they must reauthenticate or reestablish access. If a partner user launches a federated application, the timeout policy controls the following:

blocks.item: How long the session can stay active.
When idle sessions expire.
When the user must sign in again.
How long granted access remains valid from the host side.

blocks.text: Only the host partner can configure timeout policies for guest partners. The end users from the guest partner are also evaluated against the timeout policies configured by the host partner. To learn more, see Configuring Timeout Policies.

After admins complete the necessary federation configurations, shared applications are immediately available for guest users. Unlike traditional B2B solutions that require complex access procedures, Private Access B2B Federation provides a seamless and frictionless experience for the end user.
The end user experience provides the following key access behaviors:

blocks.item: Persistent corporate connection: End users remain connected to their own corporate Zscaler Client Connector at all times.
Native authentication: Zscaler Client Connector authentication remains tied exclusively to the user's home (corporate) partner identity (i.e., the guest partner's identity).

Simultaneous multi-tenant acess: Users can access shared applications hosted across multiple Private Access partner tenants simultaneously. This requires no reauthentication, profile switching, or changing of the user context.

blocks.text: From the end user's perspective, accessing a federated application feels identical to accessing an internal corporate application. When you access a shared application, the following workflow applies:

blocks.item: The user authenticates into Zscaler Client Connector using their standard corporate (guest tenant) credentials. Zscaler Client Connector authentication is always tied to the guest partner's IdP.
The user navigates to the shared application.

Private Access automatically routes the user's traffic to the host partner's application transparently in the background. The user is granted immediate network-level access without any additional Zscaler Client Connector prompts or configuration steps.

Private Access handles the secure network delivery, but it does not manage application-level authentication. If the shared application requires its own login (e.g., application single sign-on (SSO) or local credentials), the user authenticates according to the application's native security requirements.

blocks.text: B2B Federation transforms how organizations manage cross-tenant collaboration by replacing legacy network-centric connectivity with a high-performance, identity-based Zero Trust framework. The following are B2B Federation business impacts and outcomes:

blocks.item: Key Business Challenges Addressed
Accelerated speed to value: Reduces the time to establish B2B partner access from 30 to 90 days (i.e., the standard for legacy VPN or MPLS) to less than one hour.

Mergers & acquisitions and divestiture agility: Enables day-one productivity during mergers by allowing entities to remain independent while securely sharing resources. Streamlines divestitures by simply revoking federation tokens without rearchitecting the network.
Elimination of legacy costs: Removes the need for expensive network plumbing, such as MPLS, site-to-site VPNs, and dedicated firewall rules.
Strategic Alignment
Unified Zero Trust architecture: Consolidates all user access (internal and B2B) under a single platform, enforcing consistent security policies and eliminating vendor sprawl.
Scalability without complexity: Supports rapid growth and concurrent access to multiple Private Access tenants without requiring additional hardware or resource-heavy configurations.
Organizational sovereignty: Maintains the host tenant's ultimate authority over application security while empowering guest tenants to manage their own user life cycles.
Quantifiable Value
The following table provides the quantifiable metrics and business benefits for B2B Federation:

table: Reduces partner onboarding from months to minutes.
Reduce the infrastructure cost by eliminating site-to-site VPN tunnels and firewalls.

blocks.item: Enhanced User and Admin Experience
Seamless end user access: Users stay logged in to their corporate Zscaler Client Connector and access partner applications simultaneously without reauthentication or switching contexts.

Real-time governance: Provides shared transaction logs to both host and guest tenants, ensuring complete auditability and faster troubleshooting for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) or SOC teams.
Dynamic control: Admins can instantly pause or terminate federation, immediately dropping all active connections to protect sensitive assets during a security incident.

blocks.text: This section outlines compliance requirements for customers utilizing the B2B Federation feature in Private Access. Customers are solely responsible for ensuring the federation setup aligns with compliance requirements, applicable laws, and internal security policies. The following compliance requirements apply:

blocks.item: Federation Setup and Verification
Customers bear full responsibility for verifying and assessing the compliance status of their partners (external tenants) prior to configuring federation and sharing applications.

Before federating applications, customers should evaluate whether their partner is compliant with the organization's requirements for a specific application. Zscaler does not validate or restrict federation access based on compliance status.
Cross-Compliance Federation Awareness
A federation can exist between higher and lower compliance environments. For example:

A federation can exist between a FedRAMP High and FedRAMP Moderate environment. The host partner must validate their guest partner compliance profile and ensure only applications that meet FedRAMP Moderate requirements are federated. Higher-compliance applications (i.e., within FedRAMP High environments) must not be shared with a lower-compliance tenant.
A federation can exist between a federal and commercial environment. Federal tenants must not share regulated applications or higher-compliance applications with a lower-compliance commercial tenant.

It is the responsibility of the higher compliance tenant (e.g., FedRAMP High) to ensure that applications shared with a lower compliance environment (e.g., FedRAMP Moderate) remain within applicable compliance boundaries. Zscaler does not impose restrictions on this federation configuration, but the responsibility lies with the host to avoid violations.
Restrictions and Application Sharing

Zscaler does not inherently restrict or block federation access between partners (Private Access tenants) based on compliance requirements. It is the responsibility of the customers to decide if sharing sensitive data is acceptable under their regulatory obligations. You must ensure that higher compliance tenants do not share sensitive or regulated applications with lower-compliance tenants if doing so risks non-compliance or regulatory violations.

blocks.text: B2B Federation supports email notifications for events. To learn more, see About Notifications and Configuring Notifications.

To prevent the inadvertent sharing of sensitive data, logging data as part of the Log Streaming Service (LSS) is obfuscated before sharing resources between companies. The following information applies to obfuscated logs:

blocks.item: Data processing: The only new piece of metadata added to logs is partner information. However, some of the data attributes are excluded appropriately before being distributed to the relevant partner.

Split-log copies with redaction: There are two copies of the relevant log data generated: one copy goes to the guest partner, and the other goes to the host partner. Each copy excludes some of the data attributes to remove proprietary or sensitive information belonging to the other party (e.g., the host's App Connector IP addresses are removed from guest logs, and the guest's user metadata is removed from host logs). Each party's relevant log data is stored in their respective regions.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About the Log Streaming Service.
